12178503.text: Fritz, the number one seed in Stockholm, beat Norrie to reach the quarterfinals, closing out the match with his 13th ace. Norrie started well, dictating with his forehand, including a forehand winner up the line, and hitting good returns. Fritz grew into the match as his forehand warmed up, stepping in to take it early and serving well out wide. Fritz saved two set points and then took the first set 7-5. He was focused from the start and showed no ill effects from his previous tournament in Paris.

12178671.text: Musetti won 6-1 6-4 in 71 minutes, starting brilliantly and striking the ball cleanly off both forehand and backhand, with several strong volleys. Samuel had already played three matches during the week. He made some solid defensive plays but could not match Musetti, who took the first set and then broke early in the second, helped by a ball that clipped the net and dropped over.

12178945.text: Shevchenko, a qualifier from Kazakhstan, beat defending champion Ruud 6-7, 6-4, 6-3 to reach his first quarterfinal in Stockholm. Ruud won the first set in a tiebreak after a turnaround, sealing it with a shot that came more off the frame than the strings. The balls were said to get rough after six or seven games, which made winners hard to hit. The turning point came in the second set, when Ruud had two break points for a 4-2 lead and could not take them. Shevchenko responded well, seemed to have plenty of time on the ball, hit strong forehands and moved on quickly from setbacks. He came back to take the second set and then the match, finishing with a backhand.

12178957.text: Tabilo, the number four seed from Chile, beat Sonego 7-6 6-7 7-5 in Stockholm to reach the quarterfinal after just under three hours of play in which serve dominated. Sonego had come through qualifying, so he had played extra matches before this one, and his forehand was a strong weapon from the opening game. He often used it to push Tabilo off balance and then came forward to finish points at the net. The match had several close exchanges at the net and a number of drop shots, though at least one drop shot from Tabilo was well short of good enough. Sonego had a match point but missed an overhead, and Tabilo went on to win the deciding set.

12179122.text: Kecmanovic and Rune played the last match of the day in Stockholm, late at night, on the same court where Rune had played 12 months earlier. Rune made many errors from the start and finished the first set with 14 unforced errors, while Kecmanovic hit hard off the forehand and did not have to do much to win the set with a double break. Rune followed one slow first serve to the net and was passed by a Kecmanovic forehand. The match turned after Rune made his first break early in the second set, and from then on he hardly missed a ball, returned very well and used his serve to set up points. Rune completed the comeback to reach the quarter-finals, where he will face the number one seed Fritz.

12179386.text: Tabilo beat Michelsen 7-5 7-6 to reach the semi-final in Stockholm, his first indoor semi-final, a day after a three-set win. Tabilo used the drop shot well and was strong at the net, with good volleys and a well-placed lob that set up a winning overhead. Michelsen broke first in the opening set and saved two break-back points, but Tabilo broke back on his third chance and came from behind to win the set. Michelsen's forehand worked well, finishing several points and producing back-to-back winners, and he also showed good touch on the volley. The second set was tight, and Tabilo got out of trouble on his own serve before winning it, as the slightly better player against a Michelsen who pushed him hard.

12179396.text: Musetti played with strapping under his right knee. Humbert attacked throughout, hitting the ball very hard at times and mixing in a delicate change of pace, while Musetti defended from deep behind the baseline and still found winners, several of them off the backhand. The first set lasted about an hour and the match went to a deciding set in Stockholm. Musetti won to reach the semifinals, with an outstanding lob bringing up match point.

12179510.text: Tirante won to reach his first semi-final in Stockholm and his second of the year, after a hard fight against Shevchenko. Shevchenko had a tight turnaround after a match that ended around quarter past ten the night before. Tirante took the first set in a tiebreak on his fourth set point, having failed to convert four break points earlier in the set, while Shevchenko could not earn a single break point in that period. Tirante hit hard on the forehand and mixed it with drop shots, and his defence often turned into attack. Shevchenko kept fighting with belief even when behind and won the second set, but the match ran over two hours without the best quality. Tirante got the only break of serve in the deciding set and finished the match with an ace.

12179750.text: Tirante beat Tabilo 7-5, 7-6 in Stockholm to reach his first tour-level final, at his third attempt. Tirante was dominant on serve early, dropping just one point in his first service games and his net play was excellent as he moved forward at the earliest chance and finished points there. Tabilo showed good touch and used the whole court but at times his shot choices were unclear and some of his volleys were not good enough to win the point. A single break of serve decided the first set. In the second set Tirante had a chance to serve out the match but could not take it because of nerves, then won the tiebreak.

12179838.text: Fritz, the top seed, beat the third seed Musetti 6-4 6-2 in the semi-final in Stockholm. Fritz played with aggression from the start, stepping in to take the ball early. The key break came in the third game and Fritz served very well while keeping Musetti under pressure. His forehand produced many winners and he finished with 24 winners as Musetti had no answer to his attack. His tactics worked throughout and he reached his sixth final of the year and his first in Stockholm.
